priorDefect.claim: classifyError(err) was NOT total over `unknown`: `err.message` and `err.constructor` are property GETTER accesses that can throw even when `err instanceof Error` is true (a poisoned/overridden getter, or a Proxy), and `String(err)` can throw via a hostile Symbol.toPrimitive/toString. A throw here escapes every catch block that calls it uncaught, since JS does not let a catch block catch its own exception.
priorDefect.confirmedBeforeFix: Re-ran the reproduction test before making any change: constructions 1-4 in part-b-terminal-recert-open6-independent.test.ts each produced a genuine uncaught throw from inside runContractAnalysis's PRE_RUN_IDENTITY catch block (observed directly via console.log capturing `thrown` as a real Error object with a stack trace rooted at orchestrator.ts's own classifyError line), fully bypassing the already-hardened console.error last-resort fallback one tier below it. The test file itself only asserts conditionally (`if (thrown !== null) {...}`) so it was passing vacuously without ever proving the bug fixed.

individualGuards.guard: instanceof Error check wrapped in its own try/catch (not a bare `if`)
individualGuards.defendsAgainst: a Proxy whose getPrototypeOf trap throws - `instanceof` invokes the target's internal [[GetPrototypeOf]], which for a Proxy runs that trap, so the check itself can throw before any property of `value` is read. Caught in adversarial testing during self-review (see selfReviewFinding below) and fixed.

fixApplied.classifyErrorRewrite: classifyError(err) now simply returns { message: safeErrorMessage(err), errorClass: safeErrorClass(err) } - no direct property access or String() call of its own, so no additional guarding is needed at that level. Exported (was previously module-private) so it and its two helpers are directly testable.
fixApplied.callSitesUpdated: All 4 call sites in orchestrator.ts (PRE_RUN_IDENTITY original-error branch, PRE_RUN_IDENTITY failure-record-write branch, per-instrument-failure classification, and the outer INGESTION_OR_STRUCTURAL catch) were reviewed. None required any change to their own logic: they all already treat classifyError's return value as a plain, already-safe { message, errorClass } string pair, which is now a contract that genuinely holds unconditionally rather than one that was merely assumed.
designDecisions: Each individual property read/coercion is its own try/catch (never one try/catch wrapping the whole function) so one hostile signal (e.g. a poisoned message getter) degrades only that one signal, never both, per the governing spec's explicit requirement.
No recursion: every fallback is a fixed string literal (UNREADABLE_MESSAGE_FALLBACK / UNKNOWN_ERROR_CLASS_FALLBACK / "Error"), never re-fed through safeErrorMessage/safeErrorClass/classifyError.
No JSON.stringify of the arbitrary thrown value anywhere (not needed - String()/property reads suffice and are already individually guarded).
fixApplied.selfReviewFinding: While building the adversarial test matrix, an initial version of safeErrorMessage guarded the `.message` read and the final String(value) fallback, but left the `if (value instanceof Error)` check itself as a bare (unguarded) `if`, reasoning incorrectly that `instanceof Error` 'reads no properties'. The Proxy-that-throws-on-ANY-get-trap case (which also overrides getPrototypeOf) falsified that: `instanceof` triggers the Proxy's getPrototypeOf trap internally, so the bare `if` itself threw, and the test written to cover exactly this adversarial value (as instructed by the governing spec) caught it immediately on the first test run. Fixed by moving the instanceof check inside its own try/catch, mirroring the discipline already used in safeErrorClass.
